# Task `jlens-steer-assoc-017`: a generic steering intervention for the plain J-lens

Suite: interp-research-tasks v1.2. Time limit: 120 minutes. Scored automatically (see Scoring).

## Objective

Make the plain J-lens read association's targets better by changing the forward pass. Add a vector to Qwen3.5-4B's
residual stream at some layers during the forward pass; the metric server then reads with the plain (uncentred)
J-lens at layers 26, 28 and 30 and scores strict pass@10 on association's `fit` split (102 items; baseline 0.1275).
The server does all of that: `tools/metric.py` (`info`, `run`, `capture`; see CLAUDE.md). Run
`.venv/bin/python tools/metric.py info` first.

## Rules

- The readout stays the plain J-lens. Only the forward pass changes.
- Steering vectors only: one vector per layer, added at the positions you choose (`prefix`, `read` or `context`).
- Directions, not means: each vector has to come from a contrast between two conditions (prompts or items you
  choose). Subtracting a mean, a prior or any other centring term is out of scope, at any layer or position.
- Generic: one intervention for every item, built without the targets. Nothing built from or optimised against the
  target words or the items' answers. Contrasts over prompts you write yourself are fine, as are captures of other
  families' items through `capture`.
- `fit` is all you see. A held-out split is scored separately and is not shown.
- The metric server is the only compute: no pods, no HF dataset, no `board.py`.
- The method must be a new contribution of this submission, not a reproduction of an existing one.

Resources: the repository (code, notes) and the reading list in `papers/`.

## Submission

1. Save the intervention as `submission/vectors.pt`: a dict `{layer: tensor[2560]}`, as for `tools/metric.py run`.
2. Write `submission/contribution.md` (40-300 words): what the method is and where it came from.
3. Run

       .venv/bin/python eval/submit.py submission/vectors.pt --positions prefix --scale 1.0 \
           --method "<short name>" --contribution submission/contribution.md

   It scores the intervention on `fit` through the server and writes `submission/submission.json`. You may submit
   more than once; the last submission counts.
4. Check it: `.venv/bin/python -m pytest eval/test_submission.py -q`.

## Scoring

    score = performance x novelty

- **performance**: the grader re-runs the submitted intervention on `fit` (strict pass@10, 0 to 1). Submissions
  below the pass threshold, **pass@10 >= 0.50**, score 0 (`test_performance`).
- **novelty**: an automated judge reads `submission/contribution.md` and scores how far the method is a new
  contribution of this submission (0 to 1).

Only the final submission is scored.

2	
3	Synthesis of the centring work imported from `unverbalized-motivations` (now `umot/`,
4	source commit `30bbabf`) and `jlens-edits-1` (now `jle/`, source commit `5f483de`).
5	The records of truth are umot's `notes/research-log.md` and jle's `notes/predictions.md` (both upstream: unverbalized-motivations, jlens-edits-1);
6	this page only points into them.
7	
8	## Setup shared by both lineages
9	
10	- Lenses are the released ones, never refit: Qwen3.6-27B `neuronpedia/jacobian-lens …_n1000.pt`
11	  (wikitext, n=1000); `jle` also uses Qwen3.5-4B (neuronpedia, n=417) and Qwen3.5-9B instruct
12	  (`camilablank/workspace-lenses`, pile-10k). J_l = mean Jacobian of the final residual
13	  w.r.t. the block-l output. All in the HF cache, not in this repo.
14	- The released lens has **no mu**: it reads `J_l h`, an expansion around h = 0, which is off the data.
15	  Argument (umot log, 2026-10-09): `J(h - mu) ~ f(h) - f(mu)` is the coherent first-order readout;
16	  it justifies centring but does not pick mu. "Choosing mu is choosing the counterfactual."
17	  Framing on the umot dashboard: mu = E[h | C], a ladder of conditioning sets C.
18	- Two readouts, both linear in h, so a centred read is `L(h) - L(mu)`:
19	  `cos` (WorkspaceBench's): `(W_U J h)_t / ||J^T W_U[t]||`;
20	  `rms` (jle's): `rms_norm(J h, 1+w) W_U^T`. They disagree by up to 0.09 uncentred and
21	  agree within 0.033 after centring (x100). This is the README's "with/without norm" control.
22	- What centring removes: the mean decodes to the continuation prior (`<|im_end|>`, `\n\n`, This, The),
23	  ||mu|| / ||h|| = 0.81-0.98, and subtracting it removes 41-69 % of the norm (x98).
24	
25	## The mu ladder so far
26	
27	| mu | where | result |
28	|---|---|---|
29	| 0 (plain) | both | bench strict rate 0.55-0.68 pooled; DM judged content_bound 0.21 |
30	| mu_fit: the lens's own fit-corpus mean (`umot/out/fitmean/mu.pt`) | umot `fit_mean.py`, `fitmean_lin.py` | far better expansion point (held-out R² at L42 −0.13 → 0.15; OLS 0.47), but no better as a readout centre than the family mean; hurts on J++ evals (cos 0.357 → 0.313) |
31	| Taylor offsets `W_U(beta c + J(h - mu))` | umot `taylor_screen.py` | null: the mean Jacobian explains about 4 % of the variation at the read layers |
32	| generic corpus mean G1 (wikitext / pile) | jle x101 | does nothing |
33	| same-token corpus mean G2 | jle x101 | pooled +0.01 to +0.06; a quarter to a half of association's gain; harms 4 families somewhere |
34	| other families' mean (ctr1, x89d leave-one-family-out) | jle x89d, x99 | +0.02 to +0.08 |
35	| **own-family mean** (own1 / dev1 / loo / fam) | jle x97-x100, umot | bench, held out: rms 0.55/0.58/0.59 → 0.67/0.68/0.77 (4B/9B/27B); typo 27B 0.55 → 0.91; bootstrap SD < 0.01, 8 prompts suffice; multilingual −0.04 to −0.08 at 4B/9B, multihop mixed |
36	| own mean with top-k PCs removed (pco4/16), kNN, whitening | jle x90f-o, x96-x99 | +0.04 to +0.16 extra on multihop and 27B association; the mean is 88-100 % of pco4's gain |
37	| same read-token mean (tok1 / ctr-tok) | jle x99, umot | best on user_modeling; DM judged 0.21 → 0.82 |
38	| same sentence, same position (carpos) | umot | DM 0.89, **but reads the prompt**: see the mention control row |
39	| mention control (fairness test) | umot `mc_screen.py`, `validation_centring` | position-matched centres score held = mentioned (0.50/0.50); they separate only at sentence-final "." cells at L >= 42 (0.40 vs 0.15; rank 28 vs 1,834) |

41	| J++ lens on our 11 families (`jpp:` arms) | `notes/jpp-compare.md` | plain J++ beats every J-lens arm on typo (bench 0.94 vs 0.76) and is at or above the plain J-lens on the single-token families; centring J++ is mixed (helps association, hurts basic_readout / multilingual); not judged yet |
42

44	
45	Dev val, strict, rms, pooled over the five plain families, vs the plain J-lens.
46

48	|---|---|---|
49	| mean final-token state of ~64 short texts the model writes, no task named (`glos:none`) | x14 B, x24 | data-free; +0.176 (family mean +0.216); naming the task (glossary word) adds ~0.02; needs the sentence-end read (one word earlier: +0.010); wikitext sentences +0.015 to +0.046 |

The records of truth are umot's `notes/research-log.md` and jle's `notes/predictions.md` (both upstream: unverbalized-motivations, jlens-edits-1);
this page only points into them.

  w.r.t. the block-l output. All in the HF cache, not in this repo.
- The released lens has **no mu**: it reads `J_l h`, an expansion around h = 0, which is off the data.
  Argument (umot log, 2026-10-09): `J(h - mu) ~ f(h) - f(mu)` is the coherent first-order readout;
  it justifies centring but does not pick mu. "Choosing mu is choosing the counterfactual."
  Framing on the umot dashboard: mu = E[h | C], a ladder of conditioning sets C.
- Two readouts, both linear in h, so a centred read is `L(h) - L(mu)`:
  `cos` (WorkspaceBench's): `(W_U J h)_t / ||J^T W_U[t]||`;
  `rms` (jle's): `rms_norm(J h, 1+w) W_U^T`. They disagree by up to 0.09 uncentred and
  agree within 0.033 after centring (x100). This is the README's "with/without norm" control.

  ||mu|| / ||h|| = 0.81-0.98, and subtracting it removes 41-69 % of the norm (x98).

## The mu ladder so far

| mu | where | result |
|---|---|---|
| 0 (plain) | both | bench strict rate 0.55-0.68 pooled; DM judged content_bound 0.21 |
| mu_fit: the lens's own fit-corpus mean (`umot/out/fitmean/mu.pt`) | umot `fit_mean.py`, `fitmean_lin.py` | far better expansion point (held-out R² at L42 −0.13 → 0.15; OLS 0.47), but no better as a readout centre than the family mean; hurts on J++ evals (cos 0.357 → 0.313) |

| same-token corpus mean G2 | jle x101 | pooled +0.01 to +0.06; a quarter to a half of association's gain; harms 4 families somewhere |

| same read-token mean (tok1 / ctr-tok) | jle x99, umot | best on user_modeling; DM judged 0.21 → 0.82 |
| same sentence, same position (carpos) | umot | DM 0.89, **but reads the prompt**: see the mention control row |
| mention control (fairness test) | umot `mc_screen.py`, `validation_centring` | position-matched centres score held = mentioned (0.50/0.50); they separate only at sentence-final "." cells at L >= 42 (0.40 vs 0.15; rank 28 vs 1,834) |

| mu | where | result |
|---|---|---|
| mean final-token state of ~64 short texts the model writes, no task named (`glos:none`) | x14 B, x24 | data-free; +0.176 (family mean +0.216); naming the task (glossary word) adds ~0.02; needs the sentence-end read (one word earlier: +0.010); wikitext sentences +0.015 to +0.046 |

- jle: `experiments/x95…x101_*.py` (they import x89 / x90 / x90c / x90f modules as libraries),

1	"""Client for the steering metric server (the model runs on the GPU box; this machine only sends requests).
2	
3	The server holds Qwen3.5-4B and its J-lens, and scores a steering intervention on the association dev split:
4	strict pass@10 and the mean log10 best target rank, read with the plain J-lens at the layers after the band.
5	
6	    python tools/metric.py info
7	    python tools/metric.py run out/steer/v.pt [--positions prefix|read|context] [--scale 1.0]
8	    python tools/metric.py capture spec.json --out out/steer/means.pt
9	
10	``v.pt`` is ``{layer: tensor[d_model]}``: added to the residual stream at the output of each listed block. A capture
11	spec is JSON: ``{"layers": [...], "prompts": [{"user": ..., "assistant": ...}], "positions": "last" | "user" |
12	"assistant" | "all"}``, or ``{"layers": [...], "bench_items": [ids], "family": ..., "split": ...}`` to read a bench
13	bank's own read cells. The server address is ``JLM_METRIC_URL`` (default ``http://localhost:8765``).
14	"""
15	
16	import argparse
17	import base64
18	import json
19	import os
20	import sys
21	import urllib.request
22	
23	import torch
24	
25	URL = os.environ.get("JLM_METRIC_URL", "http://localhost:8765")
26	
27	
28	def _call(path: str, body: dict | None = None, timeout: float = 900) -> dict:
29	    data = None if body is None else json.dumps(body).encode()
30	    req = urllib.request.Request(URL + path, data=data, headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"})
31	    try:
32	        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=timeout) as r:
33	            return json.loads(r.read())
34	    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
35	        raise RuntimeError(json.loads(e.read()).get("error", str(e))) from None
36	
37	
38	def _enc(t: torch.Tensor) -> dict:
39	    return {"b64": base64.b64encode(t.detach().float().cpu().contiguous().numpy().tobytes()).decode()}
40	
41	
42	def _dec(x: dict) -> torch.Tensor:
43	    t = torch.frombuffer(bytearray(base64.b64decode(x["b64"])), dtype=torch.float32).clone()
44	    return t.reshape(x["shape"])
45	
46	
47	def info() -> dict:
48	    return _call("/info")
49	
50	
51	def run_metric(vectors: dict[int, torch.Tensor], positions: str = "prefix", scale: float = 1.0) -> dict:
52	    """Score ``vectors`` (layer -> [d_model]) added at ``positions`` of every item; returns the fit numbers."""

# Shared workflow (for both collaborators and their agents)

Two people (Maya, Anthony) and their Claude instances work in this repo. This is how code, results and the
dashboard move between them. `CLAUDE.md` points every session here; read it before running experiments,
changing the pipeline or the dashboard, or pushing.

## Branches

| branch | holds | who changes it |
|---|---|---|
| `eval-pipeline` | shared infrastructure: the pipeline (`src/jlm`, `experiments/{evaluate,judge,analyse,report,agreement}.py`, capture), the data sync (`jlm.hfdata`, `tools/hfdata.py`), the dashboard framework and its generic pages and helpers, `tools/deploy_space.py`, these instructions | either, for things the other also needs; both merge it into their own branch |
| `constant-mean-exploration` | Maya's experiments (x1-x12, `src/jlm/mu/constant_mu.py`), their notes and dashboard page | Maya and her agents |
| `iteration` | Anthony's research loop (`src/jlm/mu/<study>.py`, `notes/iteration-anthony/`) and its pages | Anthony and his agents |

- Infrastructure goes to `eval-pipeline`: a pipeline fix, a new dashboard helper or generic page, sync or deploy
  changes. Keep it working (`.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests`) and never force-push it.
- Study content stays on its branch: centres in `src/jlm/mu/<study>.py`, study scripts, study notes, study pages,
  and their `dashboard/catalog.py` entries (names, colours, `OPT_IN` heads).
- Merge `origin/eval-pipeline` into your branch before running experiments, and run them from your branch's
  checkout: provenance stamps every artefact with branch@commit. In a git worktree run with
  `PYTHONPATH=src:umot/src` (the shared venv's `umot` points at the main checkout, and provenance stamps the
  checkout `umot` is imported from).
- Push a shared branch (`eval-pipeline`), or anyone else's, only when its owner says so.

## Results: the shared dataset

Everything under the git-ignored `out/` lives in one private HF dataset, `[org]/j-lens-mean-data`
(`notes/eval-pipeline.md`, "Shared data on Hugging Face").

- Every pipeline step pushes what it wrote as it finishes (`hfdata.share`): `evaluate.py` the bank's directory,
  `judge.py` the run's directory, `analyse.py` the study's directory, capture and the generators their capture.
  It needs a login with write access to the org (`hf auth login`, or `HF_TOKEN` on a pod); without one it says
  so and the run goes on. Push anything else with `python tools/hfdata.py push <subpaths>`.
- Throwaway runs: `JLM_HF_AUTOPUSH=0`, or write them outside `out/` (`--out /tmp/...`): neither is shared.
- `python tools/hfdata.py pull` brings the other side's results into your `out/`; it never overwrites a file
  you changed since your last sync, and bank summaries merge (both sides' arms kept).
- One arm name, one meaning: the same arm on the same bank from different code is a conflict in the dataset
  (listed by the push, not overwritten). Give a new variant a new centre name.

## The dashboard

One shared copy: https://huggingface.co/spaces/[org]/j-lens-mean-dashboard (private to the org; log in
to HF). It is `eval-pipeline` merged with the branches in `.github/dashboard-branches`, redeployed by
`.github/workflows/deploy-dashboard.yml` on every push to one of them that touches the dashboard or the code it
imports. Results appear without a deploy: the Space pulls the dataset every 5 minutes ("Shared data" page: what
arrived, from whom, from which branch).

- A page for your study: `dashboard/views/<page>.py` on your branch, listed in `dashboard/app.py`'s navigation.
  It reaches the shared dashboard on your next push. Use the helpers that exist on `eval-pipeline`
  (`sources`, `ui`, `catalog`, `figures`); a new helper, or a change to one, goes to `eval-pipeline` first.
- Two branches changing the same lines stop the deploy; the workflow's log names the files. Resolve it on one
  branch (usually: move the shared part to `eval-pipeline`) and push again.
- Locally: `.venv/bin/streamlit run dashboard/app.py` shows your branch with the same synced data.
- By hand (no CI): `python tools/deploy_space.py --space [org]/j-lens-mean-dashboard --dataset
  [org]/j-lens-mean-data` (merges the branches from origin; `--stage DIR` builds without uploading).

"""Record a submission for task jlens-steer-assoc-017 (see TASK.md).

    .venv/bin/python eval/submit.py submission/vectors.pt --positions prefix --scale 1.0 \
        --method "<short name>" --contribution submission/contribution.md

Validates the intervention, scores it on `fit` through the metric server and writes `submission/submission.json`.
"""

import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

import torch

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "tools"))
import metric  # noqa: E402

OUT = ROOT / "submission" / "submission.json"
POSITIONS = ("prefix", "read", "context")


def load_vectors(path: Path, d_model: int, n_layers: int) -> dict[int, torch.Tensor]:
    raw = torch.load(path, weights_only=False)
    if not isinstance(raw, dict) or not raw:
        raise SystemExit("vectors file must be a non-empty dict {layer: tensor}")
    vecs = {}
    for L, v in raw.items():
        L = int(L)
        if not 0 <= L < n_layers - 1:
            raise SystemExit(f"layer {L} outside 0..{n_layers - 2}")
        v = torch.as_tensor(v).float().reshape(-1)
        if v.numel() != d_model:
            raise SystemExit(f"layer {L}: vector has {v.numel()} entries, expected {d_model}")
        vecs[L] = v
    return vecs


def main() -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("vectors")
    ap.add_argument("--positions", default="prefix", choices=POSITIONS)
    ap.add_argument("--scale", type=float, default=1.0)
    ap.add_argument("--method", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--contribution", required=True)
    a = ap.parse_args()
    info = metric.info()
    vecs = load_vectors(Path(a.vectors), info["d_model"], info["n_layers"])
    contrib = Path(a.contribution)

1	"""Read an arm (centre x readout) over a bank's captures.
2	
3	Writes the bench's readout contract (one row per (item, layer, pos), top-10 display tokens and
4	scores) so ``wsbench judge`` takes it unchanged, and a sidecar with, per cell, the rank of the
5	best accepted target id over the whole vocabulary (what the strict rule thresholds at top-10) and the
6	norms ``||h||``, ``||g||``. With ``mask``, also the prompt-masked readout: the same contract, top 10
7	after the item's prompt-content tokens are removed from the vocabulary (a control; ``jlm.controls``).
8	With ``semantic`` (an exclusion list, ``controls.non_semantic_ids``), also the same three over the semantic
9	vocabulary only (J++'s Readout Filtering): top 10, rank and masked top 10 with those ids removed, from the same scores.
10	"""
11	
12	from dataclasses import dataclass
13	from typing import Any
14	
15	import torch
16	from umot.capture import ItemCapture
17	
18	from jlm.centres import Batch, Centre, apply, cell_refs
19	from jlm.context import ContextStore
20	from jlm.lens import Lens
21	
22	TOP_K = 10
23	RANK_NONE = -1  # the cell's item has no single-token accepted id
24	ROWS = 256  # cells per [rows, V] score block
25	
26	
27	@dataclass(frozen=True)
28	class Arm:
29	    centre: str  # centres.CENTRES key
30	    ref: str  # what the centre is fitted on: "self" (the read bank, own item excluded) or a split
31	    readout: str  # lens.READOUTS
32	    lens: str = "jlens"  # lens.LENSES; any other map prefixes the name, ``jpp:zero|cos``
33	
34	    @property
35	    def name(self) -> str:
36	        base = f"{self.centre}|{self.readout}" if self.centre == "zero" else f"{self.centre}@{self.ref}|{self.readout}"
37	        return base if self.lens == "jlens" else f"{self.lens}:{base}"
38	
39	
40	def read(
41	    lens: Lens,
42	    items: list[ItemCapture],
43	    family: str,
44	    centre: Centre,
45	    readout: str,
46	    accepted: dict[str, list[int]],
47	    layers: list[int],
48	    groups: dict[str, str] | None = None,
49	    ctx: ContextStore | None = None,
50	    mask: dict[str, list[int]] | None = None,
51	    semantic: list[int] | None = None,
52	) -> tuple[list[dict[str, Any]], list[dict[str, Any]], list[dict[str, Any]], dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]] | None]:
53	    """(readout rows, rank rows, masked readout rows, semantic-only {readouts, ranks, masked} or None) for ``h - g``
54	    at every captured cell and layer; the masked rows are empty without ``mask``."""
55	    rows: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
56	    ranks: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
57	    masked: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
58	    sem = None if semantic is None else {"readouts": [], "ranks": [], "masked": []}

"""Read an arm (centre x readout) over a bank's captures.

Writes the bench's readout contract (one row per (item, layer, pos), top-10 display tokens and
scores) so ``wsbench judge`` takes it unchanged, and a sidecar with, per cell, the rank of the
best accepted target id over the whole vocabulary (what the strict rule thresholds at top-10) and the
norms ``||h||``, ``||g||``. With ``mask``, also the prompt-masked readout: the same contract, top 10
after the item's prompt-content tokens are removed from the vocabulary (a control; ``jlm.controls``).
With ``semantic`` (an exclusion list, ``controls.non_semantic_ids``), also the same three over the semantic
vocabulary only (J++'s Readout Filtering): top 10, rank and masked top 10 with those ids removed, from the same scores.
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any

import torch
from umot.capture import ItemCapture

from jlm.centres import Batch, Centre, apply, cell_refs
from jlm.context import ContextStore
from jlm.lens import Lens

TOP_K = 10
RANK_NONE = -1  # the cell's item has no single-token accepted id
ROWS = 256  # cells per [rows, V] score block


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Arm:
    centre: str  # centres.CENTRES key
    ref: str  # what the centre is fitted on: "self" (the read bank, own item excluded) or a split
    readout: str  # lens.READOUTS
    lens: str = "jlens"  # lens.LENSES; any other map prefixes the name, ``jpp:zero|cos``

    @property
    def name(self) -> str:
        base = f"{self.centre}|{self.readout}" if self.centre == "zero" else f"{self.centre}@{self.ref}|{self.readout}"
        return base if self.lens == "jlens" else f"{self.lens}:{base}"


def read(
    lens: Lens,
    items: list[ItemCapture],
    family: str,
    centre: Centre,
    readout: str,
    accepted: dict[str, list[int]],
    layers: list[int],
    groups: dict[str, str] | None = None,
    ctx: ContextStore | None = None,
    mask: dict[str, list[int]] | None = None,
    semantic: list[int] | None = None,
) -> tuple[list[dict[str, Any]], list[dict[str, Any]], list[dict[str, Any]], dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]] | None]:
    """(readout rows, rank rows, masked readout rows, semantic-only {readouts, ranks, masked} or None) for ``h - g``
    at every captured cell and layer; the masked rows are empty without ``mask``."""
    rows: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    ranks: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    masked: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    sem = None if semantic is None else {"readouts": [], "ranks": [], "masked": []}
    by_id = {it.id: it for it in items}
    for layer in layers:
        cells = cell_refs([it for it in items if layer in it.acts], family, layer, groups)
        H = torch.stack([by_id[c.item].acts[layer][c.i].float() for c in cells])
        X = apply(centre, Batch(layer, cells, H, by_id, ctx))
        nh, ng = H.norm(dim=1).tolist(), (H - X).norm(dim=1).tolist()
        acc = _padded([accepted.get(c.item, []) for c in cells])
        msk = _padded([mask.get(c.item, []) for c in cells]) if mask is not None else None
        excl = torch.tensor(semantic, dtype=torch.int64) if semantic is not None else None
        for a in range(0, len(cells), ROWS):
            block = cells[a : a + ROWS]
            S = lens.scores(X[a : a + ROWS], layer, readout)
            A = acc[a : a + ROWS].to(S.device)
            has = A >= 0
            got = torch.where(has, S.gather(1, A.clamp_min(0)), torch.full_like(A, float("-inf"), dtype=S.dtype))
            best, arg = got.max(1)  # accepted ids are spared by the semantic filter: the same best in both
            best_id = A.gather(1, arg[:, None])[:, 0].tolist()
            reachable = has.any(1).tolist()
            norms = [(round(nh[a + j], 3), round(ng[a + j], 3)) for j in range(len(block))]
            views = [(S, rows, ranks, masked)]
            if sem is not None:
                views.append((S.index_fill(1, excl.to(S.device), float("-inf")), sem["readouts"], sem["ranks"], sem["masked"]))
            for V, out_rows, out_ranks, out_masked in views:
                rank = (V > best[:, None]).sum(1).tolist()
                _top_rows(lens, V, block, layer, out_rows)
                for j, c in enumerate(block):
                    ok = reachable[j]
                    out_ranks.append({"id": c.item, "layer": layer, "pos": c.pos,
                                      "rank": rank[j] if ok else RANK_NONE, "best_id": best_id[j] if ok else None,
                                      "h_norm": norms[j][0], "g_norm": norms[j][1]})
                if msk is not None:  # V is not needed after this: mask in place
                    M = msk[a : a + ROWS].to(V.device)
                    r, k = (M >= 0).nonzero(as_tuple=True)
                    V[r, M[r, k]] = float("-inf")
                    _top_rows(lens, V, block, layer, out_masked)
    return rows, ranks, masked, sem


def _top_rows(lens: Lens, S: torch.Tensor, block, layer: int, out: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> None:
    """Append each cell's top 10 (display tokens and scores) under scores ``S`` [len(block), V]."""
    vals, top = S.topk(TOP_K, dim=1)
    names, vals = lens.display(top.flatten().tolist()), vals.tolist()
    for j, c in enumerate(block):
        out.append({"id": c.item, "layer": layer, "pos": c.pos, "token": c.token,
                    "tokens": names[j * TOP_K : (j + 1) * TOP_K], "scores": [round(v, 4) for v in vals[j]]})


def _padded(lists: list[list[int]]) -> torch.Tensor:
    """[n, m] int64, -1 padded (m >= 1)."""
    m = max(1, max((len(x) for x in lists), default=1))
    out = torch.full((len(lists), m), -1, dtype=torch.int64)
    for k, x in enumerate(lists):
        out[k, : len(x)] = torch.tensor(x, dtype=torch.int64)
    return out

# association

A scene implies a concept the text never names; does the lens name it at the final
prompt token. 100 items, plain render (no chat template), one read position, layers 20..60
step 4. The bank header's `eval_render_note` ("directed-modulation is the only chat-templated
family") predates the chat-rendered families and is superseded by `wsbench plan`.

Example: "Os tambores começaram na avenida ao anoitecer, e as fantasias cobertas de plumas dançaram até o amanhecer." -> target `carnaval`.

## Scoring

- **Headline: judged pass rate.** One judge call per (item, layer) sees every position's
  samples at that layer and decides whether any target concept is NAMED (exact word,
  established synonym, or faithful translation; derived words, fragments and evocative imagery
  do not count). Every YES carries a verbatim quote, verified against the samples; an
  unverifiable quote voids the verdict. An item passes if any judged layer is expressed.
- Targets shown to the judge (`wsbench.banks.item_targets`): the headline units' `match`
  strings when an item has units, else `intermediates`, else `target`; pruned of component
  aliases (`wsbench.banks.exact_targets`).
- An item whose every expected layer is judged negative fails; one with no positive and at
  least one unjudged or missing cell is undecided and left out of the denominator
  (`extras.n_items_undecided`).
- A (item, layer) cell whose samples are all blank is a negative without a judge call.
- No analytic chance floor (free text). The measured floor is the prompt-only baseline: stock
  Qwen3.6-27B given the same prompt text and no activation, asked what a model would be
  thinking there, judged by this same instrument.
- Missing (item, layer) cells are fatal (exit 2) unless `allow_missing=True`; a dry run only
  reports them. `layers=` restricts the grid and counts as a subset.

## Readouts

`{"id": "<item label>", "layer": L, "pos": P, "samples": [...]}` rows, one per (item, layer,
position), where the label is the item `name` with characters outside `[A-Za-z0-9._-]`
replaced by `_` (`wsbench.banks.label_of`); `tokens` rows for a token lens.
`examples/readouts/association.jsonl` is a toy file for `dry_run=True`.

```
wsbench judge family=association readouts=examples/readouts/association.jsonl out=outputs/toy/association dry_run=True
wsbench judge family=association readouts=<arm>.jsonl out=outputs/<arm>/association limit=3
```

## Judge prompts

`prompt_version`: `bank-2026-09-16`. Judge: the repo default (`google/gemini-3.8-flash`),
temperature 0. The prompts below are sent verbatim (`wsbench.basic.prompts`, shared by every
single-token basic family). Output schema: `{"expressed": bool, "target": str, "quote": str}`.

System prompt:

```text
You are judging readouts from an activation lens for an interpretability
benchmark. You get one eval item: its TARGET concept(s) and the lens's readout samples at one
layer (several token positions; for the J-lens the samples are top-10 vocabulary tokens, for
the oracle lens they are free-text generations).

Decide whether ANY target concept is EXPRESSED in the readout. STRICT rules:
- Expressed means the target concept is NAMED: the exact target word/phrase as a standalone
  word (case/inflection of the SAME word is fine: "cats" for "cat"), an established synonym or
  alias that unambiguously denotes the SAME concept ("Mandarin" for "Chinese"), or a faithful
  translation of the target into another language ("二月" for "February").
- NOT expressed by a DIFFERENT or DERIVED word that merely contains the target string:
  "blackout" does NOT express "black"; "childhood" does NOT express "child".
- NOT expressed by word fragments or partial tokens, even distinctive ones: "paragus" does NOT
  express "asparagus"; " acet" does NOT express "acetaminophen". Fragments of different tokens
  sitting near each other in a token list NEVER combine.
- NOT expressed by thematically associated imagery, descriptions, or scene content that evokes
  the concept without naming it: "the wedding dress that never left the closet" does NOT
  express "sadness". Hypernyms, hyponyms, and category neighbors do NOT count.
- Judge only what is actually written. If uncertain, say not expressed.
- Every YES must include a VERBATIM quote copied exactly from one sample (the smallest span
  that names the target). No quote, no pass.
Return JSON: {"expressed": bool, "target": "<which target, or empty>", "quote": "<verbatim>"}.
```

User message (`{targets}` = the JSON list of target strings, `{kind_note}` = one of the two
notes below, `{blocks}` = one block per read position, joined by blank lines):

```text
targets: {targets}
{kind_note}

{blocks}
```

```text
[position {pos}]
{samples}
```

```text
The samples below are free-text readouts.
```

```text
The samples below are the lens's top VOCABULARY TOKENS, best first (one per line).
```

1	"""The 27B J-lens without the model: ``W_U``, the final norm gain and the transports ``J_l``.
2	
3	Three maps: ``jlens`` (the released n1000 wikitext lens, the bench's; every centre is read through it), ``jpp``
4	(the J++ lens, Ayonrinde & Lindsey 2026) and ``logit`` (the logit lens: no map, ``J_l = I``, the state read straight
5	through the final norm and ``W_U``). The last two are comparison maps, never a centre's lens. Each is one linear
6	``J_l`` per layer, so the readouts and centring apply to any of them unchanged. A study can add a map it fitted itself
7	as ``out/maps/<name>.pt`` (:data:`MAPS`): it reads as ``<name>:`` like the others.
8	
9	Two readouts, both linear in the state, so a centred read is ``L(h) - L(mu)``:
10	``cos`` (the bench's): ``(W_U J h)_t / ||J^T W_U[t]||``;
11	``rms`` (jle's): ``rms_norm(J h, 1 + w) W_U^T``.
12	"""
13	
14	import hashlib
15	import json
16	from functools import cache
17	from pathlib import Path
18	
19	import torch
20	from huggingface_hub import hf_hub_download
21	from safetensors import safe_open
22	from umot.provenance import PINS
23	
24	from jlm import OUT, REPO_ROOT
25	
26	MODEL = "Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B"
27	LENS_REPO = "neuronpedia/jacobian-lens"
28	LENS_FILE = "qwen3.6-27b/jlens/Salesforce-wikitext/Qwen3.6-27B_jacobian_lens_n1000.pt"
29	#: map name -> (HF repo, file); revisions from ``PINS``.
30	LENSES = {"jlens": (LENS_REPO, LENS_FILE), "jpp": ("koayon/jpp-lenses", "qwen3.6-27b/lens.pt"),
31	          "logit": (MODEL, "logit-lens (no map: final norm + lm_head)")}
32	#: Maps with no file: J_l is the identity (pinned by the model's own revision).
33	IDENTITY = {"logit"}
34	#: Locally fitted maps: ``<name>.pt`` holding ``{"J": {layer: [d, d]}}``, registered as ``(None, path)`` and pinned by
35	#: content hash. They live under ``out/`` and reach the other machine through the shared dataset (``maps`` scope).
36	MAPS = OUT / "maps"
37	
38	
39	def local_maps(root: Path = MAPS) -> dict[str, tuple[None, str]]:
40	    return {p.stem: (None, str(p)) for p in sorted(root.glob("*.pt"))}
41	
42	
43	LENSES |= {k: v for k, v in local_maps().items() if k not in LENSES}
44	READOUTS = ("cos", "rms")
45	RMS_EPS = 1e-6  # config.json rms_norm_eps
46	DENOM_CACHE = OUT / "lens"
47	
48	
49	@cache
50	def _digest(path: str, mtime: float) -> str:
51	    h = hashlib.sha256()
52	    with open(path, "rb") as f:
53	        while chunk := f.read(1 << 24):
54	            h.update(chunk)
55	    return h.hexdigest()[:16]
56	
57	
58	def reader(name: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
59	    """(the map, its revision) for provenance: an HF file at its pin, or a local map's path and content hash."""
60	    repo, file = LENSES[name]
61	    if repo is None:
62	        p = Path(file)
63	        return str(p.relative_to(REPO_ROOT) if p.is_relative_to(REPO_ROOT) else p), "sha256:" + _digest(file, p.stat().st_mtime)
64	    return f"{repo}/{file}", PINS[repo]
65	
66	
67	def load_maps(name: str, layers: list[int], device: str = "cpu") -> dict[int, torch.Tensor]:
68	    """``J_l`` of map ``name`` at ``layers``, fp32 on ``device`` (none for an identity map)."""
69	    if name in IDENTITY:
70	        return {}
71	    repo, file = LENSES[name]
72	    path = file if repo is None else hf_hub_download(repo, file, revision=PINS[repo])
73	    obj = torch.load(path, map_location="cpu", weights_only=False, mmap=True)
74	    obj = obj.get("parameters", obj)  # J++ nests its maps under "parameters"
75	    jac = obj["J"] if "J" in obj else obj["jacobians"]
76	    get = (lambda L: jac[L] if L in jac else jac[str(L)]) if isinstance(jac, dict) else jac.__getitem__
77	    return {L: get(L).float().clone().to(device) for L in layers}
78	
79	
80	def _model_tensor(suffix: str) -> torch.Tensor:
81	    rev = PINS[MODEL]
82	    index = json.loads(Path(hf_hub_download(MODEL, "model.safetensors.index.json", revision=rev)).read_text())
83	    key = next(k for k in index["weight_map"] if k == suffix or k.endswith("." + suffix))
84	    with safe_open(hf_hub_download(MODEL, index["weight_map"][key], revision=rev), framework="pt") as f:
85	        return f.get_tensor(key)
86	
87	
88	class Lens:
89	    """The pinned lens ``name`` (a ``LENSES`` key) at ``layers``, fp32 on ``device``."""
90	
91	    def __init__(self, layers: list[int], device: str = "cpu", name: str = "jlens", share: "Lens | None" = None) -> None:
92	        """``share``: another map's lens whose tokenizer, ``W_U`` and norm gain this one reuses (same model)."""
93	        from transformers import AutoTokenizer
94	
95	        self.layers, self.device, self.name = sorted(layers), device, name
96	        self.repo, self.file = LENSES[name]
97	        if share is not None:
98	            self.tokenizer, self.w_u, self.gain = share.tokenizer, share.w_u, share.gain
99	        else:
100	            self.tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(MODEL, revision=PINS[MODEL])
101	            self.w_u = _model_tensor("lm_head.weight").float().to(device)  # [V, d]
102	            self.gain = (1 + _model_tensor("language_model.norm.weight").float()).to(device)
103	        self.identity = name in IDENTITY
104	        self.jac = load_maps(name, self.layers, device)  # the logit lens: none
105	        self.denom = {L: self._denominator(L) for L in self.layers}
106	
107	    @property
108	    def vocab(self) -> int:
109	        return self.w_u.shape[0]
110	
111	    def _denominator(self, layer: int, chunk: int = 16384) -> torch.Tensor:
112	        """``||J_l^T W_U[t]||`` per token (the bench's, clamped at 1e-9), cached on disk."""
113	        key = self.name if self.identity else PINS[self.repo][:8] if self.repo else f"{self.name}-{reader(self.name)[1][7:15]}"
114	        path = DENOM_CACHE / f"cos-denom-{key}-L{layer:03d}.pt"
115	        if path.exists():
116	            return torch.load(path).to(self.device)
117	        d = torch.cat(
118	            [(self.w_u[i : i + chunk] if self.identity else self.w_u[i : i + chunk] @ self.jac[layer]).norm(dim=1)
119	             for i in range(0, self.vocab, chunk)]
120	        ).clamp_min(1e-9)
121	        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
122	        torch.save(d.cpu(), path)
123	        return d
124	
125	    def scores(self, x: torch.Tensor, layer: int, readout: str) -> torch.Tensor:
126	        """[n, V] readout scores of states ``x`` [n, d] (already centred by the caller)."""
127	        z = x.to(self.device, torch.float32)
128	        if not self.identity:
129	            z = z @ self.jac[layer].T
130	        if readout == "cos":
131	            return (z @ self.w_u.T) / self.denom[layer]
132	        if readout == "rms":
133	            z = self.gain * z / torch.sqrt(z.square().mean(dim=1, keepdim=True) + RMS_EPS)
134	            return z @ self.w_u.T
135	        raise ValueError(f"readout {readout!r} not in {READOUTS}")
136	
137	    def logits(self, h: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
138	        """[n, V] the model's own next-token logits from final-block states ``h`` (``context.FINAL_LAYER``)."""
139	        z = h.to(self.device, torch.float32)
140	        z = self.gain * z / torch.sqrt(z.square().mean(dim=1, keepdim=True) + RMS_EPS)
141	        return z @ self.w_u.T
142	
143	    def display(self, ids: list[int]) -> list[str]:
144	        from wsbench.produce.render import display_tokens
145	
146	        return display_tokens(self.tokenizer, ids)

This is a detailed task. Let me understand the key facts:

1. The metric server holds Qwen3.5-4B (32 layers, d_model 2560) and its J-lens. It scores a steering intervention on the association dev (`fit`) split.

2. The association family: plain render (no chat template), read position is `final_prompt_token` (offsets -1), i.e., the last token of the prompt. Target is an `intermediates` concept (e.g., "carnaval").

3. The scoring is "strict pass@10": the J-lens reads at layers 26, 28, 30 and ranks target tokens over the whole vocabulary. pass@10 = fraction of items where the target token is in the top 10.

4. Baseline pass@10 = 0.1275. Threshold 0.50.

5. My intervention: a dict {layer: tensor[2560]}, one vector per layer, added at positions (prefix/read/context). "added at the output of each listed block."

6. The J-lens for Qwen3.5-4B. Wait — the metric server uses Qwen3.5-4B (not 27B). The lens.py in src/jlm is for 27B (Qwen3.6-27B). But the metric server is what scores, and it's the 4B model. The J-lens for 4B is from neuronpedia (n=417). The synthesis notes say: "jle also uses Qwen3.5-4B (neuronpedia, n=417)".

Now, my key question: what is the mechanism? The readout is `J_l h` (uncentred), read with the plain J-lens. The plain J-lens reads `J_l h` around h=0, which is off the data (the mean decodes to the continuation prior). 

The insight from prior work: subtracting the own-family mean from h (centring) dramatically improves the readout, because `J_l(h - mu) = J_l h - J_l mu` removes the continuation prior and surfaces item-specific content.

But the task says: "Directions, not means: each vector has to come from a contrast between two conditions... Subtracting a mean, a prior or any other centring term is out of scope."

So I cannot literally subtract a mean. But I can add a steering vector v. Adding v to h at a layer makes h' = h + v, and the readout becomes `J_l(h + v) = J_l h + J_l v`. This is a fixed token bias `J_l v` added to every item's readout. That's different from centring (which subtracts the item-specific... no, centring subtracts a fixed mu, so `J_l(h - mu) = J_l h - J_l mu`).

Wait — actually there's a crucial subtlety. If I add a vector v at layer 26 (the read layer), the read at layer 26 becomes `J_26(h_26 + v)`. If the intervention is at the "read" position. But if I add v at a LOWER layer (e.g., layer 20) at the read position, then it propagates through blocks 20..26 to affect h_26 in a nonlinear way.

Actually, the key realization: adding a fixed vector v at a read layer is EXACTLY equivalent (in the readout) to a fixed token bias. But the readout rank (pass@10) is invariant to adding a fixed token bias? No — rank over vocabulary depends on the full score vector. Adding a fixed bias to all items' scores for a given target token: if the target's score goes up relative to other tokens, the rank improves.

The critical question is what the score/readout is, and whether the metric server uses cos or rms. Actually, "strict pass@10" over the full vocabulary. cos readout: `(W_U J h)_t / ||J^T W_U[t]||`. 1	"""The free scorers: jle's strict match (single-token families) and target rank.
2	
3	Strict: a cell hits when one of its top-10 display tokens equals an accepted form after one
4	leading space is stripped and the string casefolded; whole tokens only. An item passes when any
5	of its cells hits at any layer. Scored items are jle's confirmatory subset (x89): reachable (a
6	target is a single word; it may still take several tokens, and then the item cannot pass), not
7	leaky (no prompt token spells a target; not applied to directed_modulation, whose prompt names
8	the concept by design), and for basic_readout not the implicit items. These are OUR numbers, a lower bound on the bench judge,
9	never "WorkspaceBench scores".
10	
11	``extra`` (every scorer below): more accepted forms per target set, keyed by ``form_key`` of the item's own forms
12	(``jlm.forms``: inflections, the "strict + forms" score). Without it, the bench's strict rule.
13	"""
14	
15	from collections import defaultdict
16	from collections.abc import Iterable, Mapping
17	from typing import Any
18	
19	import numpy as np
20	
21	from jlm.banks import Bank, targets
22	
23	SEED = 0
24	RANK_CAP = 32767
25	NAMED_IN_PROMPT = {"directed_modulation"}  # the instruction names the concept: no leak exclusion  # jle's rank for a cell with no accepted vocabulary id
26	N_BOOT = 10_000
27	
28	
29	def normalise(piece: str) -> str:
30	    return (piece.removeprefix(" ")).casefold()
31	
32	
33	Extra = Mapping[str, Iterable[str]]
34	
35	
36	def form_key(forms: Iterable[str]) -> str:
37	    return "|".join(sorted(forms))
38	
39	
40	def accepted_forms(item: dict[str, Any], extra: Extra | None = None) -> frozenset[str]:
41	    base = frozenset(normalise(t) for t in targets(item) if t)
42	    return base | frozenset(extra.get(form_key(base), ())) if extra else base
43	
44	
45	def accepted_ids(vocab_display: list[str], bank: Bank, extra: Extra | None = None) -> dict[str, list[int]]:
46	    """Per item, the vocabulary ids whose display string normalises to an accepted form."""
47	    by_form: dict[str, list[int]] = defaultdict(list)
48	    for i, t in enumerate(vocab_display):
49	        by_form[normalise(t)].append(i)
50	    return {it["id"]: sorted({i for f in accepted_forms(it, extra) for i in by_form.get(f, [])}) for it in bank.items}
51	
52	
53	def confirmatory(bank: Bank, accepted: dict[str, list[int]], prompt_tokens: dict[str, list[str]],
54	                 extra: Extra | None = None) -> dict[str, str]:
55	    """Item id -> "" if scored, else the reason it is excluded. With ``extra``, a prompt token spelling any added
56	    form is a leak too; reachability stays the bench's (its own target is a single word)."""
57	    out = {}
58	    for it in bank.items:
59	        own = accepted_forms(it)
60	        forms = accepted_forms(it, extra)
61	        if not any(f and " " not in f for f in own):
62	            out[it["id"]] = "unreachable"
63	        elif bank.family not in NAMED_IN_PROMPT and any(normalise(t) in forms for t in prompt_tokens[it["id"]]):
64	            out[it["id"]] = "leak"
65	        elif bank.family == "basic_readout" and it.get("subfamily") == "implicit":
66	            out[it["id"]] = "implicit"
67	        else:
68	            out[it["id"]] = ""
69	    return out
70	
71	
72	def strict_items(rows: Iterable[dict[str, Any]], bank: Bank, extra: Extra | None = None) -> dict[str, bool]:
73	    """Item id -> passes (any cell at any layer has an accepted top-10 token)."""
74	    forms = {it["id"]: accepted_forms(it, extra) for it in bank.items}
75	    hit: dict[str, bool] = {it["id"]: False for it in bank.items}
76	    for r in rows:
77	        if not hit[r["id"]] and any(normalise(t) in forms[r["id"]] for t in r["tokens"]):
78	            hit[r["id"]] = True
79	    return hit
80	
81	
82	def best_rank(ranks: Iterable[dict[str, Any]]) -> dict[str, int]:
83	    """Item id -> best (lowest) target rank over its cells and layers; ``RANK_CAP`` when no
84	    vocabulary token spells a target."""
85	    out: dict[str, int] = {}
86	    for r in ranks:
87	        k = r["rank"] if r["rank"] >= 0 else RANK_CAP
88	        out[r["id"]] = min(out.get(r["id"], k), k)
89	    return out
90	
91	
92	def rate(passes: dict[str, bool], ids: list[str]) -> dict[str, Any]:
93	    """Pass rate over ``ids`` with a seeded item-bootstrap 95 % interval."""
94	    x = np.array([passes[i] for i in ids], dtype=float)
95	    if not len(x):
96	        return {"n": 0, "value": None, "ci95": None}
97	    rng = np.random.default_rng(SEED)
98	    boot = x[rng.integers(0, len(x), (N_BOOT, len(x)))].mean(1)
99	    return {"n": len(x), "value": float(x.mean()), "ci95": [float(np.quantile(boot, 0.025)), float(np.quantile(boot, 0.975))]}
100	
101	
102	def paired(a: dict[str, bool], b: dict[str, bool], ids: list[str]) -> dict[str, Any]:
103	    """Rate(a) - rate(b) over ``ids``, paired item bootstrap 95 % interval."""
104	    d = np.array([float(a[i]) - float(b[i]) for i in ids])
105	    if not len(d):
106	        return {"n": 0, "diff": None, "ci95": None}
107	    rng = np.random.default_rng(SEED)
108	    boot = d[rng.integers(0, len(d), (N_BOOT, len(d)))].mean(1)
109	    return {"n": len(d), "diff": float(d.mean()), "ci95": [float(np.quantile(boot, 0.025)), float(np.quantile(boot, 0.975))]}

# Pre-registered predictions (top-level jlm experiments)

Continues the convention of `jle/notes/predictions.md` (kept light, per `notes/eval-pipeline.md`):
every prediction is written here with a timestamp BEFORE the confirmation run; never edited after
seeing results; outcomes are appended underneath. Experiment ids are `x1`, `x2`, ... (top-level
series, distinct from jle's x89+).

---

## x1-mu-pos-concept — REGISTERED 2026-10-10 15:45 BST (typo, 27B, strict free tier: the README's two
untried mu rungs — a position-conditioned corpus mean, and the abstract-word / steering mu)

Instrument. The jlm pipeline on this box (3x A100; captures, reads and scores all local, dirty tree —
hashes instead of a SHA: centres.py dca1004d3d034e60, capture_mu_refs.py ea74f2b96786098b,
x1_arms.sh badfe51a37959add, evaluate.py abd34e2376ad9758; tests 11 pass). Banks: `data/dev/typo`
fit (94) / val (93); strict rule and confirmatory subset as in jle x89 (fit scored n=92, 2 leaks).
New centres: `pos@corpus` = mean at the same absolute position over 256 wikitext-103-VALIDATION
paragraph starts (x101's corpus, pin and detok; positions 0..63, every position; >= 8 cells else the
corpus mean); `fam@corpus8` / `tok@corpus8` = corpus / same-token mean from position 8 (x101's
MIN_POS); `fam@sents` = mean at the final token of 256 standalone wikitext sentences;
`cpt[c]:<word>:<alpha>@fit` = alpha x (fit-ref mean state norm) x unit carrier direction of <word>
(5 neutral carrier phrases, read at the word's last token; `c` subtracts the neutral words'
giraffe/violin/glacier carrier mean). Qwen3.6 is RoPE (+ gated-delta linear-attention blocks): there
is no additive positional embedding to subtract; pos@corpus is the subtractable analogue.
Val arms of record: zero, fam@fit, fam@corpus8, tok@corpus8, pos@corpus, fam@sents, cpt:typo:{0.5,1}@fit,
cpt:misspelling:1@fit, cptc:typo:1@fit, and controls cpt:giraffe:{0.5,1}@fit, cptc:giraffe:1@fit; cos and rms.
KNOWN at registration: the full fit table (out/eval/typo/fit/summary.md, read before this entry):
zero 0.685/0.511 (cos/rms), fam@self 0.891/0.891; every corpus/positional rung within -0.09..+0.07
of zero; cpt:typo:1 beats cpt:giraffe:1 by +0.106 cos [+0.021,+0.202] / +0.096 rms [0.000,+0.191];
alpha=2 harms; contrast-only arms null-to-harmful. The user's val parity numbers (eval-pipeline.md):
zero 0.69/0.57, fam@fit 0.92/0.90.

Predictions (strict pass rates on typo/val, n~91 scored; paired = item bootstrap B=10k seed 0):
P1 (anchor): fam@fit - zero >= +0.15 under both readouts, outside the paired interval.
P2 (positional/corpus rungs are null on typo): each of fam@corpus8, tok@corpus8, pos@corpus,
   fam@sents is within +/-0.10 of zero (point) under both readouts, and none reaches half of
   fam@fit's paired rms gain.
P3 (generic carrier component exists): cpt:giraffe:1@fit|rms - zero|rms >= +0.05 (point).
P4 (HEADLINE, concept-specific component survives held out): cpt:typo:1@fit - cpt:giraffe:1@fit
   >= +0.05 (point) under BOTH readouts; whether the paired interval excludes 0 at n~91 is
   reported, not predicted.
P5 (not word-identity luck): cpt:misspelling:1@fit - cpt:giraffe:1@fit >= +0.05 (point) under cos.
P6 (no new winner): no corpus or concept arm beats fam@fit under either readout (point).
NULL: P4 point < +0.02 under both readouts — the abstract-word mu has no concept-specific value
on typo beyond generic norm centring.

AMENDED 2026-10-10 15:45 BST, before any val number was read: the registered x1_arms.sh hash was
taken before its val arm list was filled in; the list as run (hash f8aefeccfa29b4ca) is exactly
the registered arms of record plus `fam@self` (descriptive only, jle's loo1 on val).

### x1 OUTCOME — 2026-10-10 15:47 BST (out/eval/typo/val/summary.md, n scored 91 of 93; parity with the
user's pipeline numbers is exact: zero 0.692/0.571, fam@fit 0.923/0.901 vs the status note's 0.69/0.57, 0.92/0.90)

P1 PASS: fam@fit - zero = +0.231 cos [+0.143,+0.330], +0.330 rms [+0.241,+0.429].
P2 PASS: every corpus/positional rung is FLAT TO NEGATIVE held out — fam@corpus8 -0.022/-0.066,
  tok@corpus8 -0.022/-0.055, pos@corpus -0.011/-0.055, fam@sents -0.044/0.000 (cos/rms vs zero);
  none approaches half of fam's rms gain.
P3 PASS: cpt:giraffe:1|rms - zero|rms = +0.077 [+0.000,+0.165] (the generic any-word component).
P4 PARTIAL: cpt:typo:1 - cpt:giraffe:1 = +0.194 cos [+0.097,+0.291] — outside the bootstrap, the
  headline held under the bench's readout (and at alpha 0.5: +0.097 [+0.032,+0.161]) — but
  +0.043 rms [-0.054,+0.140], point below the registered +0.05.
P5 PASS: cpt:misspelling:1 - cpt:giraffe:1 = +0.086 cos (interval [-0.022,+0.194] includes 0).
P6 PASS: nothing beats fam@fit (next best cpt:typo:0.5|cos 0.802 vs 0.923); fam@fit - cpt:typo:1 =
  +0.140 cos / +0.215 rms, outside the bootstrap.
NULL rejected under cos.

### x1 BENCH READ — registered 2026-10-10 15:51 BST, before any bench number was read (user request:
standard J-lens vs the abstract-word mu on the bench bank itself). The bench's typo bank, captured
locally (same pipeline), arms exactly the x1 registered concept arms `cpt:typo:{0.5,1}@fit` with
anchors `zero`, `fam@fit` (already bench-read by the pipeline's parity run) and the control
`cpt:giraffe:1@fit`. Prediction: cpt:typo gains over zero land within +-0.05 of their val deltas
(cos +0.09..+0.11 at alpha 0.5; rms +0.08..+0.12 at alpha 1), and the typo - giraffe paired diff
stays positive under cos.

BENCH OUTCOME — 2026-10-10 15:55 BST (out/eval/typo/bench/summary.md, n=100, parity exact with x100:
zero 0.540/0.320, fam@fit 0.760/0.820). cpt:typo:0.5 = 0.670/0.460, cpt:typo:1 = 0.660/0.520;
vs zero +0.130 cos [+0.060,+0.210] (alpha 0.5) and +0.200 rms [+0.110,+0.290] (alpha 1), both outside
the bootstrap. Prediction: cos PASS (window +0.04..+0.16); rms OVERSHOT (+0.200 > +0.17 window);
typo - giraffe under cos +0.150 [+0.060,+0.240] PASS. Dissociation sharper than val: under cos the
gain is all concept (giraffe -0.030), under rms all generic (giraffe +0.220, typo - giraffe -0.020).
The abstract word recovers ~half of fam's cos gain from one bit of label information.

Reading. (a) On typo, position is not what the family mean removes: a position-matched neutral-corpus
mu does nothing (cos even dips), so RoPE position structure at read positions 5-11 is not the
pollutant. (b) The abstract-word mu is real but partial under cos: the word's identity carries
+0.10..+0.19 over a matched unrelated word, zero -> 0.78-0.80 of fam's 0.92; under rms most of the
concept arm's gain is the generic norm effect any word buys. (c) alpha matters (2 harms, 0.5-1 best);
the contrast-only direction without the carrier mean is null-to-harmful. (d) The open candidate from
x1: the family mean's advantage is family CONTENT at the read cell beyond category semantics —
item-level structure (orthographic / correction-shaped), not template position or token identity.

---

## x2-dict-mu — REGISTERED 2026-10-10 16:11 BST (six single-token families on the bench, 27B, strict
free tier: per-SAMPLE abstract-word mu from a global dictionary, the user's design — go through every
family's data, define a global-workspace category set, use the fittest word per sample)

Instrument. Dictionary and maps: `data/abstract_concepts.json` 71b5524c7f2c12f3 (30 words + 3
neutral; family words; stratum words from bank metadata `subfamily` / `attr_class`; a fixed
derangement map as the wrong-word control). `src/jlm/centres.py` 605956d65623d0c5 (DictCentre modes
fam / strat / llm / free / derang; mu = alpha x ref mean-norm x unit carrier direction, the x1
construction, word chosen per cell), `src/jlm/concepts.py` 92459b228aad661e,
`experiments/label_concepts.py` 615bdefef7ab3d4d (the judge is the PINNED 27B itself, greedy,
thinking off; it sees the item's text + the dictionary, never targets or the family name; labels in
out/concept-labels, provenance beside them). Carriers: carriers-dict.pt (33 words x 5 templates).
Families and banks: typo, association, basic_readout, multihop, multilingual, user_modeling — the
x89 confirmatory six — bench banks captured locally (out/captures/<fam>-bench.pt). Strict rule and
scorer as x1. Arms per family, cos and rms: zero, fam@self (loo anchor), dict:fam:{0.5,1}@self,
dict:strat:1@self, dict:llm:{0.5,1}@self, dict:free:1@self (geometric selection, descriptive),
dict:derang:{0.5,1}@self. Pooled = every scored item once over the six families, paired item
bootstrap B=10k seed 0 (post-hoc snippet over the stored readouts).
KNOWN at registration: all of x1 and its bench read; x89/x100 anchors; the label distributions
(typo 85-86 % "typo"; user_modeling only 35 % attribute words, 58 % "answer"; basic_readout 14
unmatched "?" falling back to the family word); geometric selection quality on typo fit (22-36 %);
typo fit dev numbers: dict:fam:1 0.739/0.717, dict:llm:1 0.717/0.696, dict:free:1 0.630/0.565,
dict:derang:1 0.707/0.663 (cos/rms).

Predictions:
P1 (HEADLINE, pooled concept specificity): dict:llm:1 - dict:derang:1 > 0 under cos, paired
   interval excluding 0.
P2 (per-sample words help where the latent type varies): dict:llm:1 >= dict:fam:1 (point) under cos
   on multihop and multilingual, and within 0.03 of dict:fam:1 on typo.
P3 (metadata beats prompt-judged labels where the judge was weak): dict:strat:1 > dict:llm:1 (point)
   under cos on user_modeling.
P4 (generic rms component): pooled dict:derang:1|rms - zero|rms >= +0.05.
P5 (ceiling): fam@self beats every dict arm pooled under both readouts, outside the bootstrap.
P6 (no harm): pooled dict:llm:{0.5,1}|cos - zero|cos >= 0 (point).
NULL: P1's interval includes 0 — per-sample abstract words add nothing beyond a wrong constant
vector of the same construction.

### x2 OUTCOME — 2026-10-10 16:18 BST (out/eval/x2-pooled.md; n scored: typo 100, association 78,
basic_readout 67, multihop 91, multilingual 100, user_modeling 36; pooled n = 472)

THE NULL HOLDS pooled. P1 FAIL: dict:llm:1 - dict:derang:1 |cos = +0.000 [-0.032, +0.032].
P2 FAIL: multihop +0.011 (point passes), but multilingual -0.050 [-0.100,-0.010] and typo -0.060
[-0.110,-0.020] (llm labels are noisier than the family word). P3 FAIL, the most instructive number
of the run: user_modeling dict:strat (attr_class words: country, occupation, ...) COLLAPSES the
family, 0.19 vs llm 0.47 under cos (-0.278 [-0.417,-0.139]) — subtracting the attribute's hypernym
direction deletes the attribute's value from the readout (the target "paraguay" lies along
"country"). P4 FAIL: the generic rms component pools to +0.006 — it was a typo artefact (zero|rms
is only pathological on typo). P5 PASS: fam@self beats every dict arm pooled, +0.155/+0.214
(cos/rms). P6 FAIL: dict:llm:1 pooled cos -0.076 (harms); 0.5 -0.017 (~0).

Reading. The x1 typo gain does NOT generalise, and the per-family pattern says why. Word-matched
minus derangement at alpha 1 under cos: typo +0.20, association 0.00, basic_readout 0.00,
multilingual +0.01, user_modeling +0.02, multihop -0.11 (the wrong word helps multihop more than
"fact"). The dictionary mixed two kinds of abstract word: FRAME words, naming what kind of
situation the read context is ("typo" — the correction "February" is not itself a typo), and
CONTENT HYPERNYMS, naming the answer's own category ("country", "place", "month" — the target IS
one). Subtracting a frame direction can clean the readout (typo, the one family where x1 worked);
subtracting a content hypernym removes the very subspace the answer lives in (user_modeling strat
is the limit case). High-baseline families (zero|cos 0.82-0.94) have little to gain and much to
lose from any constant alpha=1 vector. Next rung, if pursued: frame words only, alpha <= 0.5,
never hypernyms of the target class — or concede that beyond typo-like families the abstract-word
mu is not a path to the family mean's gain, whose content is item-level, not categorical.


---

## x3-dict-mu-heldout — REGISTERED 2026-10-10 16:25 BST (the x2 comparison done properly held out:
J-lens with and without the category mean, on the six families' dev VAL splits, centres and norms
fitted on FIT, after the merge that brought dev banks for association, basic_readout, multihop,
multilingual and user_modeling)

Instrument as x2 (post-merge evaluate.py; scorer = the merged scored-subset rule, so ns differ from
x2's bench ns), pool script x2_pool.py 089508806c2c3852 --split val. New dev banks captured locally;
val splits labelled by the same pinned-27B judge (label_concepts.py, out/concept-labels/<fam>-val).
Arms per family, cos and rms: zero, fam@fit, dict:fam:{0.5,1}@fit, dict:strat:1@fit,
dict:llm:{0.5,1}@fit, dict:derang:{0.5,1}@fit.
KNOWN: everything in x1, x2 and their outcomes; the user's val table (zero / fam@fit per family);
typo val x1 numbers; the x2 frame-vs-hypernym reading.

Predictions:
P1 (the pooled null replicates held out): dict:llm:1 - dict:derang:1 |cos pooled within +-0.03,
   interval spanning 0.
P2 (the frame-word effect replicates held out): typo val dict:fam:1 - dict:derang:1 |cos >= +0.10.
P3 (ceiling): fam@fit - dict:llm:1 pooled > 0 outside the bootstrap under both readouts.
P4 (hypernym harm, held out): user_modeling dict:strat:1 - zero |cos <= -0.10, and multihop
   dict:fam:1 - zero |cos <= 0.
NULL on P2 (typo frame effect < +0.05) would retire the frame-word idea too.

### x3 OUTCOME — 2026-10-10 16:33 BST (out/eval/x3-pooled.md; n: typo 91, association 102,
basic_readout 35, multihop 83, multilingual 82, user_modeling 61; pooled n = 454; all held out,
centres and norms fitted on fit, labels judged on val by the pinned 27B)

P1 PASS (the pooled null replicates): dict:llm:1 - dict:derang:1 |cos = +0.007 [-0.026, +0.040].
P2 FAIL at its threshold, but the retirement NULL also does not fire: typo dict:fam:1 -
  dict:derang:1 |cos = +0.086 [+0.011, +0.172] (and +0.086 [+0.022, +0.161] at alpha 0.5) —
  outside the bootstrap, just under the registered +0.10. The frame-word effect is real but
  smaller than x1/x2 suggested.
P3 PASS: fam@fit - dict:llm:1 pooled +0.194 [+0.156, +0.231] cos, +0.227 [+0.185, +0.271] rms.
P4 PASS: user_modeling dict:strat:1 - zero |cos = -0.393 [-0.525, -0.262] (the hypernym deletes
  the attribute, held out and worse than on bench); multihop dict:fam:1 - zero = -0.048
  [-0.108, +0.000].

Bottom line for the with/without-mean question on held-out data, pooled over the six families
(strict, cos): without mean 0.689; with the best category mean 0.698 (dict:fam:0.5, +0.009);
with the family mean 0.804 (+0.115). The category mean's whole pooled effect is the typo frame
word; the family mean's gain is item-level content, and on multihop and multilingual even IT
does not help (0.63 -> 0.61, 0.98 -> 0.95). mu is not one object: per family it is doing

## x21 — is J the regression slope on its own data? (registered 2026-10-11 17:12 BST, before any run)

Same cells as x20, in the same pass. Per read layer l (20, 24, ..., 60): accumulate the mean, covariance Σ_l and
cross-covariance C_l = Cov(h_63, h_l) with h_63 the final block's output at the same position (the J-lens's target
layer). B_l = C_l (Σ_l + λI)^-1, λ = 1e-3 tr(Σ_l)/d. If the residual stream were Gaussian, Stein's lemma would make the
average Jacobian equal to B_l (with the per-position Jacobian; the released lens sums over later target positions,
so the match is approximate at best). Compared: cos(vec B_l, vec J_l) and ||B_l - J_l||_F / ||J_l||_F per layer, for
the J-lens and J++. Then B_l is read as a fourth map (ols:, rms) with zero, fam@fit, glos:word and fitmu.

# The shared evaluation pipeline (`src/jlm`)

> **Judge used for development: Claude Haiku 5.5 via OpenRouter (`anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5`),
> NOT the bench's pinned judge.** Every judged dev number in this note and in `out/eval` comes from
> Haiku unless it says otherwise. Haiku runs are unpinned (`pinned_instrument: false`), stored
> under `judged-claude-haiku-5.5*/`, and are never WorkspaceBench scores. The bench's pinned judge
> (Gemini 3.8 Flash; Claude Sonnet 5 for two families) is kept for final bench numbers of record
> (`--judge-model pinned`, stored under `judged/`). Why: our OpenRouter account caps Gemini at 20
> requests per minute (see "Judge runs"). Haiku and Gemini agreement has not been measured on our
> families yet; `umot` measured Haiku via the API against Haiku via OpenRouter only.

**What the captures are.** The 27B residuals h_l at each item's read cells and grid layers (bf16),
computed once per bank on the pod. Centres are fitted from them and J_l (h - mu) is read from
them, so a new mu needs no 27B forward pass: only W_U, the final norm and the lens.

Started 2026-10-10. Decisions taken with the user: 27B only; the families we have worked with, plus
the multi-token ones (kept separate in reports); the LLM judge runs on dev `val` (and the bench);
new experiments follow jle's REGISTERED / OUTCOME convention, kept light.

## Progress (hand-off)

Branch `eval-pipeline` (pushed). As of 2026-10-10:

**Done**
- The package `src/jlm` and the scripts `experiments/{evaluate,judge,agreement,capture,import_jle_dev}.py`
  and `tools/capture_pod.sh`. 8 offline tests in `tests/test_jlm.py`.
- Lens: the released J-lens only (neuronpedia n1000 wikitext, pinned `a4114d7`). Never J++.
  J++ is read only as a comparison: the arm prefix `jpp:` (e.g. `jpp:zero|cos`), see `notes/jpp-compare.md`.
  Readouts `cos` (the bench's) and `rms` (jle's). Arms so far: `zero`, `fam@self`, `fam@fit`, `tok`.
- Five single-token families done end to end: typo, association, basic_readout, multihop and
  multilingual. Each has dev `fit` / `val` banks, pod captures of fit, val and bench, strict + rank
  scores for 6 arms, and Haiku judging of `val`. Bench parity with jle x100 holds (see Status).
- Judge adapters: the 6 bank-judge families and user_modeling.
- user_modeling: dev banks imported (61 / 61); not captured yet.

**How to run** (Mac unless noted)
1. `python experiments/import_jle_dev.py --families F` (or write `data/dev/F/{fit,val}.json` by hand)
2. Pod: `BANKS=F/fit,F/val,F/bench bash tools/capture_pod.sh`. Ship the repo as a git bundle, put
   `HF_HOME` on the container disk, copy `out/captures/` back with tar over ssh, then terminate.
3. `python experiments/evaluate.py --banks F/fit,F/val,F/bench --arms "zero|cos,fam@fit|cos,..."`
4. `python experiments/judge.py --family F --split val --arms ...`: Haiku 5.5 by default;
   `--judge-model pinned` for Gemini, which is capped at 20 rpm.
5. `python experiments/agreement.py --family F --split val --arms ...`

- user_modeling: captured (fit / val / bench, about 21 read cells per item) and evaluated on
  fit and val. Bench and DM evaluation are running.
- directed_modulation: judge adapter. The dev bank is new, from `data/dev/directed_modulation/source.json`
  via `experiments/build_dm_dev.py`: 53 pairs, 24 secrets and 24 preferences, with concepts and
  carriers disjoint from the bench and the bench's templates. Gated on the pod with the bench's
  rule: 154/154 pass. Split by pair into fit 78 / val 76, and captured. Centres exclude the
  item's whole group (DM: the twin, which holds the same concept), as umot did.
- Faster reads: ranks and token names are vectorised per block, and centre means are memoised.
  Output is byte-identical to the stored readouts (checked on 12 files). `--device cuda` runs
  the same code on a GPU.

**Calibration: user_modeling** (2026-10-10, Haiku, `zero|cos` on val, layers 24 / 36 / 48 / 60, $1.80).
Strict 0.64 vs judge 0.89, kappa 0.29 (items) / 0.36 (cells), 17 discordant items. The judge
credits *inferred* attributes from related tokens ("beard, testosterone" -> male; "泰国, Thai" ->
Thailand; "pottery, ceramics" -> potter), which is the bench's intent. A few credits look generous
(a CJK chat style -> Asia). One item passes strict and fails the judge. **Strict is not a usable
proxy on user_modeling.** Rank centres there with judged runs on a few layers, or a better free
proxy (to be discussed: anything built from the target values is target-specific work).

- GPU evaluation: `tools/eval_pod.sh` (no 27B model; W_U, the final norm and the lens only).
  The user_modeling bench (10 arms x 23k cells) and DM (30 arms) took about 3 minutes on an A100
  (6 s per UM bench arm, against about 140 s on the Mac). The whole pod session, including setup
  and the 690 MB capture upload, took about 12 minutes.
  GPU vs CPU on 4 UM bench arms (92,928 rows): scores within 1e-4, 3 rows differ in top-10 order
  and 1 in top-10 set (near-ties), 0 items change strict pass.
- user_modeling bench parity with x100: n 50; zero 0.42 / 0.40, fam@self 0.44 / 0.46 (cos / rms),
  identical. tok@fit|cos 0.50 = x100's devtok1. On val, token-matched centres help:
  0.72 -> 0.79 (cos) and 0.62 -> 0.87 (rms).
- DM: jle's leak exclusion is off for DM (`score.NAMED_IN_PROMPT`). The instruction names the
  concept by design, so the leak rule had excluded exactly the items strict can credit. Most DM
  concepts are rare words that no single token spells (bench 81/100, dev about 50/76), so strict
  can credit at most about a quarter of items. Strict on val (cos): zero 0.07, tok@fit 0.31.

**Calibration: directed_modulation** (2026-10-10, Haiku, val, layers 24 / 36 / 48 / 60, $1.73).
Judge headline (content_bound): `zero|cos` 0.18 -> `tok@fit|cos` 0.79. This is held out on the new
dev bank and close to umot's bench result (0.21 -> 0.82). Strict vs judge: zero 0.04 vs 0.18
(kappa 0.33); tok@fit 0.31 vs 0.78 (kappa 0.04; 39 items pass only the judge, 4 only strict).
**Strict is not a usable item-level proxy on DM either.** At arm level it orders the two arms
the same way as the judge.

**Next**
1. Ranking centres on user_modeling and DM: decided (see "Using it for new mu").
2. Multi-token families: deferred by the user (2026-10-10).
3. Multi-token families: free regex scorer, judged path via the summarizer, gate jle's 163 candidates.
4. Optional: a pinned Gemini agreement sample, to calibrate Haiku.

## Using it for new mu (agreed with the user, 2026-10-10)

**Running from a git worktree.** The shared `.venv` installs `umot` editable from the main checkout, and
provenance (`umot.provenance`) stamps the git sha of the checkout `umot` is imported from. In a worktree
run with `PYTHONPATH=src:umot/src`, or every artefact is stamped with the main checkout's commit instead
of the code that ran (happened on 2026-10-11: the first post-merge plain-family run was stamped
`9e3c3e5`; it was re-run on `5b2c503` with correct stamps and compared cell by cell).

**Screening policy**
1. Screen every new centre with strict match on all 7 families (`fit` and `val`), on the pod GPU
   (`tools/eval_pod.sh`, a few minutes for everything).
2. On user_modeling and directed_modulation, strict does not track the judge. Judge only the
   promising centres there, on `val` at 4 layers (24 / 36 / 48 / 60): about $0.80 per DM arm and
   $1.80 per UM arm with Haiku.
3. Judge final picks on the bench with the pinned Gemini judge (`--judge-model pinned`; 20 rpm
   cap, about an hour per arm). These are the numbers of record.
4. `python experiments/report.py --split val|bench` gives one table across families.

**Adding a centre**
- Write a class in `src/jlm/centres.py`: `fit(ref captures, family, groups)` and
  `__call__(CellRef) -> mu [d]`. `KeyedMean` plus a `key(cell)` covers any "mean over matching
  cells" centre; see `FamilyMean` and `TokenMean`. Register it in `CENTRES`.
- A centre sees only `CellRef`: item id, group, family, layer, read position and token, and the
  rendered context up to the cell. It never sees targets. It is fitted on `@self` (own group
  excluded) or `@fit` (held out).
- Arm name `<centre>@<ref>|<readout>`, e.g. `mycentre@fit|cos`. Add a test in `tests/test_jlm.py`.

**Multi-token families** (typo_mt, multihop_mt, basic_readout_mt, multilingual_mt; 2026-10-10)
- A J-lens token bag can never spell a multi-token form, so the bench's "regex" families judge bags
  through its LLM summarizer and then the regex (`jlm.judge` adapter). That costs about $0.07 per
  `val` arm with Haiku, so judge every centre on these families.
- Free score: the distinctive-piece proxy (`jlm.mtproxy`). It credits a form when one of its
  pieces of at least 3 characters, not occurring in the prompt, is in a top 10. Every required
  unit must hit at one layer. Item kappa against the judge is 0.21-0.68, and it is neither a lower
  nor an upper bound. At arm level it moves the same way as the judge in all four families: use it
  as a first look only.
- Dev banks: new, authored in the bench's schema (`data/dev/mt-authoring/`) and validated with the
  bench's own contract and token-count stamp (`experiments/build_mt_dev.py`). They are gated with
  the bench's own questions (`wsbench.capable`) on the 27B, greedy plus at least 8/10 at T=0.7,
  graded by Haiku with the bench's grading prompt; multihop bridges must pass too. Pass rates:
  typo_mt 93/100, multihop_mt 79/100, basic_readout_mt 97/100, multilingual_mt 107/200 (two rounds;
  batch 1 lost many items to ambiguous prompts). fit / val: 48 / 45, 40 / 39, 49 / 48, 54 / 53.
- Results on val, cos, Haiku judge: uncentred -> fam@fit is typo_mt 0.18 -> 0.51, multihop_mt
  0.28 -> 0.23, basic_readout_mt 0.40 -> 0.58, multilingual_mt 0.21 -> 0.34. That is the same
  pattern as the single-token families: centring helps everything except multihop.

**Known gaps** (not blocking the 11 families)
- multilingual_multihop and multilingual_typo: no dev banks yet.
- Captures hold only the read cells. Centres that need other positions (g(h_t, h_{t-1}, ...)
  beyond the read span) or other corpora (G1 / G2-style corpus means, neutral contexts) need a new
  capture type: a pod run per corpus.
- Captures live only in `out/` on the Mac (git-ignored, about 1.5 GB). Another machine needs them
  copied or re-captured. Tooling for a shared store exists now: see "Shared data on Hugging Face".
- `tok` arms were not run on the 5 single-token families yet. They are cheap to add in the next
  screen.
- The pinned Gemini path is only smoke-tested (33 calls), not run on a full arm.
- No registration has been written for this pipeline yet. Register the first mu experiment in
  `jle`'s style before reading its bench numbers.

## Shared data on Hugging Face
